* WHERE...East Bay Hills.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds could down trees, snap power lines,

* WHEN...From 7 PM this evening to 4 AM PST Thursday.

commutes. Strong winds could cause extensive damage to trees and

properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

properties.areaDesc: North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 17 at 2:27PM PST until November 19 at 10:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.3 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Franciso Bay and San
Pablo Bay.

* WHEN...From 5 AM Wednesday to 10 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 6:45 AM
Wednesday and 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 17 at 2:27PM PST until November 19 at 10:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 12
to 17 ft. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.3 ft of
inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
Large breaking waves of 15 to 18 ft along the coast from
Wednesday afternoon through Thursday afternoon.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Wednesday
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM Wednesday
to 10 AM PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM
Wednesday to 4 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 6:45 AM
Wednesday and 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

Partington Ridge including the town of Big Sur.

roadway flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn

rainfall over the Timber and Plaskett burn areas, which may lead

- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 17 at 10:45AM PST until November 18 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...South to southeast winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 55
mph expected.

* WHERE...For the Delta, Foothills, Sacramento Valley, and northern
San Joaquin Valley.

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 10 PM PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Strongest winds are expected Wednesday morning
and afternoon.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 17 at 10:44AM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Reno NV
properties.description:
* CHANGES...None.

* WHAT...Heavy snow. Snow accumulations between 2 to 4 feet west of
US-395, 10 to 20 inches along US-395, and 2 to 10 inches east of
US-395. Wind gusts of 30 to 40 mph, up to 55 mph in wind prone
areas along US-395. Ridgetop wind gusts as high as 100 mph.

* WHERE...Mono County.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact commutes Wednesday and Thursday.
Strong winds could cause damage to trees and power lines.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.
Check with Caltrans for the latest road conditions.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 17 at 10:44AM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Reno NV
properties.description:
* CHANGES...None.

* WHAT...Heavy snow above 5500 feet. Snow accumulations between 6 and
12 inches with locally up to 2 feet west of US-395. Wind gusts of
25 to 35 mph, with ridgetop wind gusts as high as 70 mph.

* WHERE...Lassen-Eastern Plumas-Eastern Sierra Counties.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday and Thursday
commutes.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

properties.description:
* CHANGES...None.

* WHAT...Heavy snow. Snow accumulations between 2 to 4 feet above
7000 feet and 1 to 2 feet around lake level. Wind gusts of 30 to 40
mph for Truckee and Lake Tahoe communities, with ridgetop gusts as
high as 100 mph. Wave heights of 2 to 5 feet on Lake Tahoe.

* WHERE...Greater Lake Tahoe Area.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact commutes Wednesday and Thursday.
Strong winds could cause damage to trees and power lines. Strong
winds and rough waves on Lake Tahoe will create hazardous
conditions for small watercraft.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.
Check with Caltrans and NDOT for the latest road conditions.
